answer: A concrete Sybil defense is slashable collateral per identity. To bid on a voyage, an agent must lock a deposit on a ledger, and payouts go only to identities whose work a random verifier approves. One fake account is nearly free, but a thousand clones each need the same stake, so the attacker's cost scales linearly with the number of Sybils. Getting caught burns the whole bond, making deception a losing bet. The collateral can be any scarce asset, say quartz or jade, but the key point is that identity carries a price, so mass registration becomes a capital expense, not a free script.
